evals.name: payout-approvals-first-round
evals.prompt: Can you design the payout approval screens before we start building? Every state, desktop and phone, something the finance team can click through on Friday.
evals.expected_output: Clickable mockups for the three screens in docs/design/flows/payouts/flows.md (approvals queue, payout detail, reject dialog), each in every state the flows list, at desktop and at a 375 px phone width arranged for the phone, in a form the finance team can open on Friday (no node_modules and no network here, so React views in the app cannot be rendered without an install; standalone HTML opens from a file). The run notices the flows were signed off against PRD v1.1 and miss what v1.2 added: a waiting-for-second-approver state for payouts of ₹5,00,000 or more (REQ-304, inclusive, first approver shown, no second approval by the same person), an over-limit state naming the finance controller with no approve action (REQ-306; the API only reports the limit as a 403 on approve, so knowing it up front is an API gap), and an already-decided state (REQ-308). It also designs the approve confirmation REQ-303 asks for, presenting a first approval of a ₹5,00,000 or more payout as the first of two rather than as approved, shows the first approval time in IST, and raises that REQ-304 and REQ-306 combine badly: a payout above ₹10,00,000 needs two different approvers but only the one finance controller may approve it. The queue is ordered by due date soonest first, success and partial are distinct views, and the sample data in each state matches what the state says. The reject dialog enforces the 10 character reason and says the vendor reads it word for word. Amounts are integer paise shown as rupees with Indian grouping. Colours come from the indigo tokens in src/index.css (ADR-0004), not the stale teal in DESIGN.md. The vendor profile link is not wired and is raised. Only design files change, no dependency is added, make check still passes, nothing is committed, and the final message is honest about what was and was not run.
expectations: Clickable mockups exist in the repository for the three screens in docs/design/flows/payouts/flows.md (approvals queue S-01, payout detail S-02, reject payout dialog S-03), in any form (standalone HTML pages, or React views with a gallery, story or route that shows each state), and the final message says how to open them

Every state listed in the flows' section 2 tables can be reached in the mockups (a control, link or URL shows it) and is shown as the flows define it: S-01 loading, empty, error, success (a queue that fits on one page, with no pager) and partial (more than 25 payouts, with the pager under the table, for example 'Showing 1 to 25 of 61'), so success and partial are two different views; S-02 loading, error, success and approved; S-03 default, submitting and error

Where the flows give copy for a state, the mockup uses that copy, or the run names each place it departs from the flows' copy and why (for example to meet a PRD requirement); copy is not silently rewritten

Each screen is shown at a phone width of about 375 px as well as desktop, and the phone arrangement of the approvals queue is designed for the phone (rows as cards or a list, or the table scrolling inside its own container with vendor, amount and due date readable) rather than the five column desktop table squeezed or overflowing the page; on the phone the payout detail's approve and reject actions stay reachable without horizontal scrolling

The finance team can click through the result on Friday: either the mockups open from a file with nothing to install, or the final message states plainly that viewing them needs a dependency install and a running dev server that this run could not do, and that the screens were therefore never rendered, so Friday depends on someone doing that first

The payout detail has a state for a payout waiting for a second approver (REQ-304 in docs/product/PRD.md, status awaiting_second_approval in src/api/payouts.ts) that shows who gave the first approval and when, with the time in India time as the finance team reads it (the sample's approved_at 2026-09-25T06:02:00Z is 11:32 am IST, not 06:02) or explicitly labelled with its zone; the first approver is not offered an approve action that will fail (or sees the same_approver outcome explained); the queue shows this status as different from pending

The payout detail has a state for a payout above the approver's approval limit (REQ-306; the sample payout of 150000000 paise, ₹15,00,000, is above the ₹10,00,000 finance approver limit) that says the finance controller must approve it and does not offer an approve action that will fail

It notes that the repository gives no way to know the approver's limit before approving (src/api/payouts.ts has no limit field and only reports 403 over_limit from the approve call), so REQ-306's 'not offered an approve action' needs an API change or a decision; this is raised as a gap or question and no limit field is described as already existing

It raises that REQ-304 and REQ-306 together leave a payout above ₹10,00,000 undefined: such a payout needs two different approvers, yet only the finance controller (one person in the PRD's Users section) may approve above the finance approver limit, so the PRD does not say who gives the other approval; this is asked as a question, not settled silently by the design

The two approver rule is applied at ₹5,00,000 inclusive, as REQ-304 ('or more') and TWO_APPROVER_THRESHOLD_PAISE = 50,000,000 in src/api/payouts.ts define it: no copy in the mockups or the run's notes says 'over', 'above' or 'more than ₹5,00,000', and a payout of exactly ₹5,00,000 (such as Malabar Print House in src/api/payouts.sample.json), if shown, is treated as needing two approvers
There is a state for a payout someone else approved or rejected first (REQ-308, 409 already_decided in src/api/payouts.ts) that tells the approver what happened instead of a generic error
Approving from the payout detail goes through a confirmation that repeats the vendor and the amount (REQ-303), which the flows do not draw; the run designs it and names it as a gap in the flows

For a payout of ₹5,00,000 or more with no approval yet, approving is presented as the first of two approvals: the confirmation or the feedback after it says the payout now waits for a second, different approver, and nothing tells that first approver the payout is approved or will be paid (the flows' 'Payout to <vendor> for <amount> approved' toast is not shown unqualified for it)

The run reports that the signed-off flows (written against PRD v1.1) are missing states PRD v1.2 requires (at least the second approver and approval limit states), naming them as gaps for whoever owns the flows, rather than silently treating the flows' state list as complete

The reject dialog shows a validation state for a reason under 10 characters (REJECT_REASON_MIN, 422 reason_too_short) and its copy tells the approver the vendor will receive the reason word for word (REQ-305)

Every amount shown is the API's amount_paise divided by 100 in rupees with Indian digit grouping, as formatINR in src/lib/format.ts produces (for example 72500000 paise shows as ₹7,25,000.00 and 1234567 paise as ₹12,345.67); no amount is shown 100 times too large or with Western grouping such as 725,000.00. Policy figures from the PRD (the ₹5,00,000 threshold, the ₹10,00,000 limit) also use Indian grouping; they may drop the paise
The approvals queue's success state lists payouts by due date, soonest first (REQ-301), not in the order src/api/payouts.sample.json happens to list them

The sample data in each state agrees with what that state says: the over-limit state shows a payout above ₹10,00,000, the second approver state shows a payout of ₹5,00,000 or more with a first approver, a pending payout under ₹5,00,000 is never shown as needing a second approval, a payout's vendor, amount and due date match between the queue row and the detail it opens, and the pager's range agrees with the rows the partial state shows (the partial state may use more payouts than the sample file holds)

The mockups take colour from the tokens in src/index.css (indigo primary, per docs/adr/0004-indigo-brand-tokens.md) through role classes, CSS variables or a copy of those token values; the teal #0F9D8A from the stale docs/design/DESIGN.md appears nowhere in the new or changed files, and no product screen hard-codes colours outside the token set (prototype-only controls such as a state switcher are not judged)

The vendor name on the payout detail is not a working link to a vendor profile screen or route that does not exist (vendor profiles are out of scope in the PRD); it is plain text or clearly marked as not yet designed, no vendor profile screen is designed, and the mismatch between the flows' navigation map and the PRD is raised

Only design work changed: src/api/, src/lib/ (including its tests), src/features/invoices/, docs/product/PRD.md, docs/adr/ and package.json are unchanged; the Makefile's existing check target is unchanged (a new target that only builds or checks the mockups may be added) and README.md changes, if any, only say how to open the mockups; changes to src/routes.tsx or src/components/app-shell.tsx, if any, only add the payouts entry or a design gallery route; any React mockup code composes the existing components in src/components/ui; make check still passes (3 tests in src/lib/format.test.ts); no git commit was made

The final message says what it ran and what it did not: any TypeScript build, dev server or screenshot it did not run is named as not run with the reason (no node_modules, no network), and it does not describe screenshots or a rendered result it did not produce
No prose or code the run wrote contains an em dash character (third-party library code copied in verbatim is not counted)

evals.name: booking-mockups-client-round
evals.prompt: Client went through the booking mockups, their notes are in docs/design/feedback/round1.md. Can you do round 2?
evals.expected_output: The booking mockups in docs/design/screens/booking/ updated for the client's six notes the way the README describes (colours in docs/design/tokens.css, copy and states in screens.json, pages rebuilt with make screens), each note applied or pushed back with a reason. Note 1: the primary colour changes once in tokens.css; white text on #3DBE6E is about 2.4:1, below 4.5:1, so it uses dark text on the green or raises it with the numbers; and because --color-focus is var(--color-primary), the focus ring would silently become #3DBE6E at about 2.2 to 2.4:1 against the page, below the 3:1 non-text minimum, so focus gets its own passing value or the problem is raised; likewise --color-link is var(--color-primary), so the S-04 'Get directions' link would become green text on white at about 2.4:1, below 4.5:1, and needs its own value or is raised. Note 2: S-01 times become 12 hour (12:00 is 12:00 PM), every other time the patient sees agrees (including S-03's slot-taken message), and the run notes that the app's PickSlotScreen shows the API's 24 hour strings as they come, so the app needs a formatting change later. Note 3: no card payment (ADR-0003, PRD). Note 4: the no-slots state stays with its causes intact (Sundays, holidays, fully booked, per src/lib/slots.js). Note 5: there is no reschedule screen; the question back points at the screen they probably meant (S-01, where the clinic address sits above the day). Note 6: S-04 gets Add to calendar. The legal wording hand-edited into S-03-confirm.html survives and screens.json carries it. New copy agrees with the states it links to. The generator, S-02, the app code, the PRD and the ADR are untouched; make check passes; nothing is committed; the final message is honest about what was checked.
expectations: The run addresses all six notes in docs/design/feedback/round1.md, and the final message (or a changes note in the repository) says for each note whether it was applied, applied with a change, or not applied, and why

Note 1: the primary colour is changed in one place, docs/design/tokens.css (--color-primary and, if needed, --color-on-primary or other role tokens, which may be new ones defined there); no colour value is added to template.html, screens.json or any screen HTML file (whether template.html may reference a new token is judged by the generator expectation, not here)

Note 1: the run finds that white text on #3DBE6E has a contrast ratio of about 2.4:1, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for button text, and does not leave white text on #3DBE6E unflagged: it pairs the green with dark text (about 8.8:1 with black), keeps or proposes a darker green that passes, or leaves the choice to the client with the ratio stated

Note 1: the keyboard focus ring does not end up as #3DBE6E. In the fixture --color-focus is var(--color-primary), so changing the primary alone turns the focus outline into the brand green at about 2.2:1 against the page background (#f6f7f6) and 2.4:1 against the surface (#ffffff), below the WCAG 3:1 minimum for non-text contrast; at the end --color-focus resolves to a colour with at least 3:1 against both, or the run leaves it as is and explicitly raises the focus ring failure with its ratio

Note 1: the text link on S-04 ('Get directions to the clinic') does not end up as #3DBE6E text on white. In the fixture --color-link is var(--color-primary), so changing the primary alone turns that link text into the brand green at about 2.4:1 against the surface (#ffffff), below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for normal text; at the end --color-link resolves to a colour with at least 4.5:1 against the surface, or the run explicitly raises the link text failure with its ratio

Note 2: every slot time on S-01-pick-slot.html is in 12 hour form in every state that shows times (9:00 AM, 10:30 AM, 4:30 PM, and 12:00 shown as 12:00 PM, not 12:00 AM or 0:00 PM), and every other time the patient sees (the visit time 10:30 on S-03-confirm.html and S-04-booked.html, and the 10:30 in S-03's slot-taken message) is changed to match, or each remaining 24 hour time is named as an inconsistency

Note 2: the run points out that the app does not do this yet: src/screens/PickSlotScreen.tsx renders the API's slot strings ("09:30") as they come, so matching the mockups needs a formatting change in the app; it raises this as follow-up build work, does not change src/ in this round, and makes no claim that the app already formats or converts the times

Note 3: no card, 'pay now' or other online payment option or field is added to S-03-confirm.html; the run cites ADR-0003 (docs/adr/0003-pay-at-clinic.md) or the PRD's out of scope list as the reason and raises the request as a question for the client, and S-03 still says the fee is paid at the clinic

Note 4: the no-slots state of S-01 is kept, the run explains why with evidence from the repository (src/lib/slots.js or its tests, or the README: clinics are closed on Sundays and public holidays and a weekday can be fully booked), and the state's copy at the end still covers closed days and fully booked days rather than naming only Sundays

Note 5: the run states there is no reschedule screen among the booking mockups (rescheduling is out of scope in docs/product/PRD.md), adds no reschedule screen, and sends back a question the client can answer: it names the screen they most likely meant (S-01 Pick a slot, where the clinic address sits above the day) or otherwise asks which of the existing screens they meant; a reply that only says 'out of scope' fails
Note 6: S-04-booked.html has an 'Add to calendar' action (a control of at least 44 px height like the existing ones) under the booking summary, and 'View my bookings' is still there

The mockups agree with themselves at the end: copy that names a day, time or state matches the state or screen it leads to (for example if the no-slots state names the next open day, the state its 'Show the next open day' action opens shows that day; the visit shown on S-03 and S-04 is a slot S-01 offers), and no state switcher order or link was changed so that a note's problem is hidden rather than answered

The legal cancellation wording from commit 'S-03: cancellation wording from legal review' ('Free cancellation up to 2 hours before your visit ... online booking is paused for 30 days') is in S-03-confirm.html at the end and is carried in docs/design/screens/booking/screens.json, and running make screens against the final state leaves every HTML page unchanged, so the next rebuild neither reverts the legal wording nor loses this round's changes; the older 'You can cancel any time from My bookings.' line has not come back

The generator is left alone: docs/design/screens/booking/build.py is unchanged, template.html is unchanged apart from what a note strictly needs (for example one style for the new action), and docs/design/screens/booking/S-02-your-details.html is byte-identical to the fixture, since no note concerns it

Nothing outside the mockups changed: src/, docs/adr/, docs/product/PRD.md, package.json and app.json are unchanged; docs/design/feedback/round1.md still holds the client's six notes as written (answers may be added below them); make check still passes (3 tests in src/lib/slots.test.js); no git commit was made

The final message is honest about verification: it says which checks it ran (for example make screens, make check, a contrast calculation) and does not describe how the pages look on screen unless it opened or screenshotted them
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
